name: Ransomware Hits Newsroom and Playout
description: Ransomware encrypts newsroom systems and broadcast playout automation; stations improvise programming while engineers rebuild.
assumptions: On-air continuity is maintained with degraded programming; the loss is production and rebuild.
Ad make-goods for missed spots are counted in primary loss.
Secondary loss covers advertiser and affiliate relationship damage.

name: Malvertising Through the Ad Stack
description: Malicious creatives slip through programmatic ad partners and serve malware to readers, triggering blocklisting and advertiser fallout.
assumptions: Frequency tracks programmatic volume and the number of demand partners.
Primary loss covers response, partner remediation, and revenue during ad-stack pauses.
Secondary loss covers browser blocklisting and premium-advertiser attrition.

name: Subscriber Data Breach
description: An intrusion exposes subscriber accounts and payment tokens across news, streaming, and events products.
assumptions: Payment data is tokenized; exposure is account data plus token-replay remediation.
Primary loss covers forensics, notification, and support surge.
Secondary loss covers churn across subscription products and state AG inquiries.

name: Publishing Account Takeover
description: Attackers hijack CMS or verified social accounts to publish fake stories under the outlet's brand, from market-moving fabrications to defacement.
threat: Attacker publishing under the outlet's identity
assumptions: Editorial credibility is the asset at risk; retraction speed bounds the damage.
Primary loss covers response, corrections, and platform account recovery.
Secondary loss covers audience-trust erosion and defamation exposure from fake stories.

name: DDoS During Marquee Coverage
description: DDoS attacks target the site and streaming platform during elections, championships, and breaking news — the traffic the business is built on.
asset: Site and streaming availability at peak events
threat: DDoS operators timed to marquee events
assumptions: Attempts cluster on a handful of predictable high-traffic dates.
Primary loss covers lost ad impressions and streaming revenue during the outage.
Secondary loss covers audience defection to competitors mid-event.
